w3d5r1: PMs get thousands of feedback items weekly from interviews, surveys, app reviews, sales calls, support tickets and social posts. Reading it all manually is impossible.
Amplitude AI Feedback (formerly Kraftful) connects all these sources in minutes, with no engineering help, and uses agentic AI to sort the unstructured text into product categories.
It surfaces top complaints and top feature requests with counts (e.g. 96 users asking for more reliable notifications), plus deep dives into sub-themes and the original comments.
Insights turn into action: build a cohort of users who made a request, watch their session replays, or survey them to learn more.
The same insights help marketing (customers' own words for positioning) and support (common complaints to fix head-on).
w3d5r2: Mixpanel is event-centric: every user action is an event with a time, a user, and custom properties (e.g. video category, minutes watched); user profiles add descriptive properties.
Dashboards show top-line KPIs, and global filters (e.g. mobile vs web) let you slice every metric instantly, with no SQL or data team needed.
Insights report: pick an event, choose a counting method (totals vs uniques), add first-time and inline filters, compare to prior periods, and break down by properties like UTM source.
Funnels measure step-by-step conversion (e.g. app open → watch video → purchase), with views for conversion over time, time to convert, and frequency.
Flows map the unknown paths users take to a milestone; Retention shows when users drop off (e.g. below 50% around day 24–26).
w3d5r3: Spark is Mixpanel's generative-AI feature: you ask questions about your data in plain English and get a ready-made report.
Product example: "What do users do after logging in on iOS?" returns a Flows report; asking for login → search → view item → add to cart → checkout returns a funnel with drop-off per step.
Marketing example: rank campaigns by revenue contribution, then ask for return on ad spend (ROAS) per campaign.

Key principle: AI output can be verified. You can open any generated report to check its events, formulas and breakdowns, and edit it manually or by asking Spark (e.g. switch last-touch to first-touch attribution).
w3d5r5: ON DELETE SET NULL: when a referenced parent row is deleted, the foreign key in the child table becomes NULL. ON DELETE CASCADE deletes the whole child row instead.
Add these to existing tables by dropping the old foreign key constraint and re-adding it with ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... ON DELETE ....

Stored procedures save reusable SQL: CREATE PROCEDURE name(params) BEGIN ... END, run it with CALL name(...). Change the DELIMITER temporarily while creating one. Procedures can take parameters (e.g. IN id INT).
Stored procedure trade-offs: less network traffic, better performance and permission-based security, but more memory per connection.
Triggers run automatically BEFORE/AFTER an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE, FOR EACH ROW. Use NEW.col and OLD.col, e.g. auto-calculate salary from hourly pay, or keep an expenses total in sync.
